newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Oct 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning.
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's troubled political scene will add to economic problems, keep investors jittery and give no respite to the country's sagging stock markets this week, brokers say

** Delhi court to hear former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's request to quash a non-bailable arrest warrant against him in a forgery case. The warrant was temporarily stayed on Friday shortly after it was issued by a lower court
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange Index lost 153.46 points or 4.71 percent to 3101.27 in the week ending Friday
** India will soon have to lower interest rates and increase liquidity to help industrial output and prevent a feared economic slowdown, analysts say
They say industry, traders and the stock markets are eagerly looking to the government to help the economy break out of what they called a mid-year lull
** Reserve Bank of India puts cap on fresh investments in shares of State Bank of India with immediate effect since the 20 percent ceiling has been reached, the Business Standard newspaper reports
** India's Congress Party inducts chief architect of economic reforms, former finance minister Dr Manmohan Singh, into the party's top decision-making panel on Sunday
** The spot dollar/rupee INR= opens steady at 35.62/63 per dollar, dealers say
MARKETS:
** On Friday, shares across India tumbled in nervous trade with SBI leading the freefall
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index dropped 94.50 points or 2.96 percent to 3101.26
** The 100-share National index eased 44.97 points or 3.12 percent to 1394.95
** The Calcutta index shed 1.17 points to 420.37
** The Madras index fell 32.06 points to 3312.70
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is examining options for a probe into the recent price fluctuation of SBI shares, the Business Standard says

** Truckmaker TELCO has asked component manufacturers to slow down supplies for its heavy commercial vehicles, the Financial Express says adding the firm is cutting down production due to a fall in demand
** Financial institutions have asked the Essar group to give a detailed report of the group's liquidity problems and investment plans, the Financial Express says
